questions.context: In a school garden in Medellín, children see tall trees, colorful flowers and a small river.

options.text: Tree, flower and river.
options.feedback: Tree, flower and river are all words from nature.

options.text: Chair, table and book.
options.feedback: Chair, table and book are classroom objects, not nature.

options.text: Car, bus and train.
options.feedback: Car, bus and train are means of transport, not nature.

options.text: Shirt, shoes and hat.
options.feedback: Shirt, shoes and hat are clothes, not nature words.

questions.explanation: Esta pregunta repasa vocabulario esencial de la naturaleza en inglés. También ayuda a distinguir palabras del entorno natural y objetos de la vida diaria.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In a park in Bogotá, a teacher says: "Please put the plastic bottle in the recycling bin."

options.text: Throw trash in the river.
options.feedback: Throwing trash in the river pollutes nature and is wrong.

options.text: Burn all the paper.
options.feedback: Burning paper pollutes the air and is not recycling.

options.text: Use materials again to protect nature.
options.feedback: To recycle means to use paper, plastic and glass again.

options.text: Leave trash on the street.
options.feedback: Leaving trash on the street harms the city and nature.

questions.explanation: Reciclar significa reutilizar materiales para cuidar el planeta. También se practica la comprensión de instrucciones ambientales en inglés.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct sentence about the box.
questions.context: In a classroom in Cali, there is one recycling box for paper near the door.

options.text: There are one box for paper.
options.feedback: "There are" is for plural nouns, not for "one box".

options.text: There is one box for paper.
options.feedback: "There is" is correct with the singular noun "one box".

options.text: There is three boxes for paper.
options.feedback: "There is" is not correct with the plural "three boxes".

options.text: There am one box for paper.
options.feedback: "There am" is never correct in English grammar.

questions.explanation: There is se usa con sustantivos singulares como one box. También se refuerza la diferencia básica entre singular y plural en inglés.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the problem on the beach?
questions.context: In Cartagena, students read: "There are five sea turtles on the beach. There is one plastic bag near them."

options.text: There are no turtles on the beach.
options.feedback: The text says there are five sea turtles on the beach.

options.text: There are five plastic bags.
options.feedback: The text mentions only one plastic bag, not five.

options.text: There is a plastic bag near the turtles.
options.feedback: The plastic bag can hurt the turtles and pollutes the beach.

options.text: There is no water on the beach.
options.feedback: The text does not talk about water on the beach.

questions.explanation: La lectura combina there is y there are con un mensaje ambiental. También muestra cómo el plástico amenaza a los animales marinos de Colombia.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Banana peels and apple cores go in the organic bin because they are _____.
questions.context: At a school in Bucaramanga, children separate trash: paper in the gray bin and banana peels in the green bin.

options.text: plastic.
options.feedback: Plastic does not come from fruits and is not organic.

options.text: natural waste from food.
options.feedback: Fruit peels are natural waste that can become compost.

options.text: glass bottles.
options.feedback: Glass bottles are not food waste and go in another bin.

options.text: metal cans.
options.feedback: Metal cans are not organic and need a different bin.

questions.explanation: Los residuos orgánicos vienen de alimentos naturales como frutas. También se practica la clasificación correcta de basuras para reciclar en la escuela.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why is the páramo important for Colombia?
questions.context: In class in Pereira, students read: "The páramo in Colombia is cold and wet. There are frailejones and small lakes. The páramo gives water to the cities."

options.text: Because it is hot and dry.
options.feedback: The text says the páramo is cold and wet, not hot and dry.

options.text: Because there are sharks and beaches.
options.feedback: Sharks and beaches are not part of the páramo ecosystem.

options.text: Because it gives water to the cities.
options.feedback: The text says the páramo gives water to the cities.

options.text: Because it has no plants or lakes.
options.feedback: The text mentions frailejones and small lakes in the páramo.

questions.explanation: El páramo es un ecosistema único que produce agua para millones de personas. También se analiza información explícita de una lectura corta en inglés.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which rule explains the difference between the two sentences?
questions.context: In Santa Marta, a teacher writes two sentences: "There is a jaguar in the Amazon." "There are pink dolphins in the Amazon river."

options.text: "There is" is for one animal, "there are" is for more than one.
options.feedback: Singular "a jaguar" uses "is" and plural "dolphins" uses "are".

options.text: "There is" is for rivers, "there are" is for forests.
options.feedback: The place does not decide between "is" and "are".

options.text: "There is" is for big animals, "there are" is for small animals.
options.feedback: Size does not decide the verb; number decides it.

options.text: "There is" is for the past, "there are" is for the future.
options.feedback: Both sentences are in the present, not past or future.

questions.explanation: La elección entre there is y there are depende del número del sustantivo. También se conecta la gramática con animales emblemáticos de la Amazonía colombiana.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Manizales, three students propose ideas: throw batteries in the river, reuse paper at school, and plant trees in the park.

options.text: Throw batteries in the river.
options.feedback: Batteries poison water and animals, so this harms nature.

options.text: Buy more plastic bags every day.
options.feedback: More plastic bags create more trash and pollution.

options.text: Leave lights on all night.
options.feedback: Wasting electricity harms the environment and costs money.

options.text: Reuse paper and plant trees in the park.
options.feedback: Reusing and planting trees reduce trash and clean the air.

questions.explanation: Evaluar acciones permite elegir las más responsables con el ambiente. También se promueve reutilizar y sembrar árboles como hábitos sostenibles en Colombia.
questions.subject: ingles
